# Built-in loadout: fix-codex. The fix loadout with the Codex CLI as its
# writer: the same required check, the same review by a different model for
# up to three rounds, the same ADJUDICATIONS, in the same egress, hardened
# Session. The writer is the pinned Codex from the codex recipe image
# (`axocoatl recipe build codex`). Codex brings its own tools, so the writer
# lists none.
#
# credential defaults to auto: at admission the run takes codex-openai (an
# OpenAI API key, sent to api.openai.com) when it is stored, else
# codex-chatgpt (a ChatGPT sign-in from `axocoatl connect codex`, sent to
# chatgpt.com), else it is refused, saying how to connect. The run records
# the credential it chose (a note in the Outcome and the run's manifest).
# --param credential=codex-openai or codex-chatgpt chooses one.
#
# writer_model defaults to openai:gpt-6.1-sol, the first model (priority 1)
# of Codex 0.160.1's bundled model catalog, which Axocoatl's pinned table
# prices. The reviewer has no default: it is a native Agent on another model
# (Ollama or OpenRouter), and a reviewer on the writer's model is warned
# about.
#
# Budgets. Admission refuses a writer whose tokens cannot hold one model call
# of its model: 400,000 for Codex 0.160.1's models (its 272,000-token context
# plus 128,000 output tokens). Codex reports every input token of every
# request, cached input included, so one program run can report several
# million tokens; a program run that reports more tokens than its grant
# still allows fails, so tokens leaves room for the first run and the two
# revisions three review rounds can ask for. Codex has no spending stop of
# its own: each of its requests counts against invocations and the host
# stops it when they run out, and its cost, computed from the tokens it
# reports at its model's price, settles against cost_usd. The reviewer's
# budget is fix's.
schema: axocoatl.loadout/1
id: fix-codex
version: 1
name: Fix with Codex
description: >-
  The Codex CLI makes the change inside the Session; the host runs the
  required checks on the exact final files and a reviewer on a different
  model must approve the result.
kind: fix
params:
  writer_model:
    kind: model
    default: openai:gpt-6.1-sol
    description: openai:<model> that Codex runs (default openai:gpt-6.1-sol)
  reviewer_model:
    kind: model
    required: true
    description: provider:model of the reviewer, a native Agent on Ollama or OpenRouter (use a different model than the writer)
  credential:
    kind: text
    default: auto
    description: codex-openai (an OpenAI API key), codex-chatgpt (a ChatGPT sign-in) or auto (codex-openai when stored, else codex-chatgpt)
agents:
  - id: writer
    role: writer
    runtime: codex
    credential: { param: credential }
    model: { param: writer_model }
    instructions: >-
      You own this change. Find the relevant code and tests, make the change,
      run the project's check command and fix failures, then compare your diff
      with the task. When the host sends you review findings, answer every
      finding in an ADJUDICATIONS block: a line ADJUDICATIONS, then a fenced
      JSON array with one object per finding, {"id": "F1", "decision":
      "accept" or "reject", "reason": "..."}. Reject only with a concrete
      reason (the code that shows the finding is wrong). Fix each finding you
      accept, run the checks again, and give your final answer. Leave no file
      you created only for testing or debugging (scratch scripts, test binaries
      such as `go test -c` output, build outputs, reports): delete them, then
      run the project's check command one last time before your final answer.
checks:
  - name: tests
    run: { detected: true }
    timeout: 3m
review:
  model: { param: reviewer_model }
  rounds: 3
  tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob]
  adjudicate: true
  instructions: >-
    Review the change against the task and against every contract and edge
    case the docs, comments and tests describe. Read the code the change
    touches, not only the diff. Number each finding F1, F2, ... at the start
    of its line, with file:line, what is wrong and what to change; report
    only defects, not style. Give the verdict line the host asks for,
    VERDICT: APPROVE or VERDICT: CHANGES. Change nothing.
budgets:
  agent: { activations: 4, invocations: 200, tokens: 20000000, cost_usd: 10 }
  reviewer: { activations: 3, invocations: 120, tokens: 1500000, cost_usd: 3 }
  wall_clock: 60m
prompt: |
  {task}
sandbox:
  network: egress
  workload: hardened
environment:
  recipes: [codex]

def paginate(items, size):
    """Return `items` split into pages of `size` items.

    Every page but the last is full; the last page holds whatever is left.
    """
    if size <= 0:

    items = list(items)
    count = -(-len(items) // size)

def numbers(count):
